# moddotplot-rs

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

moddotplot-rs is an install-free, browser-native interactive genomic dotplot. Rust and
WebAssembly perform sequence parsing and scientific computation in a dedicated worker;
TypeScript and WebGL2 provide progressive rendering, pan, zoom, orientation coloring,
and coordinate axes. Input data remain in the browser.

> **Status:** functional preview. The core and browser workflows are tested, but the
> project is not yet labeled research-validated. See [current evidence and open
> gates](docs/STATUS.md).

## Current method

The production estimator uses canonical rolling ntHash2, undensified
one-permutation hashing (OPH), verified 32-bit register winners, HLL cardinalities,
and ModDotPlot-style maximum directed containment:

```text
C = max(containment(X core, Y expanded), containment(Y core, X expanded))
ANI_c = C^(1/k)
```

`ANI_c` is the historical ModDotPlot name for this containment-derived display score.
It is not a claim of biological average nucleotide identity or equivalence to
alignment-derived `ANI_m`. Scientific validation tests the sketch against containment
from complete canonical k-mer sets. See the
[validation contract](docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md).

The default first view uses 256 OPH registers. Completed 256-cell blocks paint while
the axes are still being prepared. After preview paint, only tiles whose quick result
is near a display decision or has weak support are refined with 1,024 registers.
HLL precision is 10. Terminal zoom uses exact canonical k-mer equality rather than
sketches and paints each match across its complete k-mer footprint.

Rejected minmer, bottom-s, alternate-hash, densified-OPH, and inverted-kernel
implementations were removed after the v0.1 baseline was tagged. Their conclusions
remain in a [historical decision record](docs/adr/0004-validated-production-backend.md).

## Features

* Load multiple FASTA records, including gzip and BGZF FASTA, without upload or installation.
* Select any loaded record independently for the X and Y axes.
* Render 500, 1,000, 2,000, or 4,000 overview cells per axis.
* Paint completed quick blocks immediately and refine uncertain tiles asynchronously.
* Pan and zoom through cached 256 by 256 tiles with coarse visual fallback.
* Switch between containment-derived `ANI_c` and support-aware orientation coloring.
* Reach an exact k-mer dotplot at terminal zoom.
* Recolor cached results with an 80% to 100% three-anchor transfer function.
* Stack local GC% and CpG tracks or imported plain/gzip/BGZF BED/GFF/GTF annotations along either axis.
* Export nonzero, detailed current-view data as BEDPE by default or CSV, using the
  native system save picker where available.
* Export the complete visible composition as PNG, SVG, or PDF; SVG and PDF keep axes,
  labels, tracks, and an outside heatmap legend as vectors while embedding the heatmap
  as a raster. Terminal exact plots use a categorical base key instead.
* Report computation progress, estimated application memory, and method provenance.

See the [user guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) for operation and interpretation and
[data export formats](docs/EXPORT_FORMATS.md) for exact BEDPE/CSV schemas and formulas.

## Build and test

Tool versions are pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.node-version`,
`web/package.json`, `Cargo.lock`, and `web/package-lock.json`. Install Rustup,
`wasm-pack`, Node/npm, and a current desktop browser, then run:

```sh
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
```

That single build command runs the TypeScript unit tests, generates the Wasm bindings,
type-checks and builds the static site, and regenerates the SBOM and license bundle.
The deployable site is written to `web/dist/`. It must be served over HTTP or HTTPS;
`file://` execution is not supported by browser module-worker security rules.

For local development:

```sh
npm --prefix web run build:wasm
npm --prefix web run dev
```

For the full verification suite:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo check -p moddotplot-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm --prefix web exec playwright install chromium firefox webkit
npm --prefix web run verify
```

`verify` includes real-Wasm Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit tests for transaction
cancellation, initial exact mode, privacy/network behavior, progressive refinement,
worker recovery, pairwise operation, keyboard navigation, and WebGL context recovery.
If Google Chrome is installed, `npm --prefix web run test:e2e:chrome` runs the same
suite in that browser.

## Repository layout

```text
crates/core       Scientific algorithms, exact oracle, and validation tests
crates/wasm       Stateful browser boundary and resource admission
web/src           UI, compute worker, renderer, axes, and caches
web/tests         Pure TypeScript unit tests
web/e2e           Real browser/Wasm integration tests
docs              Specifications, decisions, validation history, and guides
scripts           Reproducible release and dependency-inventory tools
```

The browser runtime has no third-party JavaScript library and no application server.
The dependency inventory is in [SBOM.cdx.json](SBOM.cdx.json); complete discovered
dependency license texts are bundled in
[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt), with source-level notices in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
